Why do we need a new class? This adds an extra level of redirection.
This also fails the logic of having "LogFileHandler" class.
In this proposed design, "LogFileHandler" is just acting as a passage to create instances of FileLogger, why would we need a class to do that?

Please check the next comment in continuation of this.
Done

Instead, why can't we have specific file streams initialized with respective files in the constructor here itself and specific public APIs for each file pointers based on placeholder, exposed from this class and called in Logger class as required?
Done
is it file name or is this log file path ?
Done
rotation of log only specific to class FileLogger, why this will be common to other inherited classes ?

After discussion with 
Sunny Srivastava
, we decided to keep rotation as a common feature for both FileLogger and AsyncFileLogger.
Acknowledged
can we move this to cpp file
It's supposed to be an `inline` method. I do not see any benefit of moving this to `.cpp` file.
In that case why we are not having inline mentioned here?
Methods defined in class are implicitly made `inline` by the compiler.

correct but there are two major reason behind having keyword "inline".
a) Readability
b) It gives flexibility that this header can be used in a file which already has a similar function definition without giving linker error for multiple definition.
So, its a good way to design header files with definition.

I agree about point a. But with respect to point b. this method is a private method inside `class LogFileHandler` and also in namespace `vpd`, so no chance of collision unless someone adds another private method with same signature in the class.

Anyways, I have added `inline` specifier.
can me mention, same file will be rotated after reaching max entries.
Done
can the class name be species and distinguish with other child class ex: RotatingFileLogger or LogRotator or LogFileRotator ?

After discussion with @sunnsr25@in.ibm.com, we decided to keep rotation as a common feature for both `FileLogger` and `AsyncFileLogger`. So it doesn't make sense to include "Rotator*" in the class name
Acknowledged
can we use reset() here, which is simpler than the operator=() implementation.
Done
we can move these input to constants ?
Done
don't we need collection log for single FRU VPD collection exposed buy CollectFRUVPD method ?
I think it's okay to have single FRU VPD collection go to journal as only minimal logs would be there for a single FRU VPD collection flow. @sunnsr25@in.ibm.com what's your opinion?
As discussed, we do not need to log single FRU VPD to collection log file.
we can use reset() here ?
Done
can we move these input to constants ?
Do you mean `constants.hpp` ? These are used locally by `Logger` and not required to be exposed to entire repo.
Done
can't we use logMessage(), which redirect to journal ?
Done

I also see that this commit modifies Logger class and adds two new APIs to that class but commit message does not gives info on that.

Also I would suggest, instead of updating the commit message, break the commit into parts where one commit points points to changes done in logger class and another in log file handler as thos e changes are mutually exclusive.
Lets take one class at a time?
Addressed. Please see https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/openpower-vpd-parser/+/84008
Eventually going forward all the logging will be routed via logger object? Can we have the implementation going that way and have logger object as class member?
Done
What is the idea behind these levels? How are we going to use it going forward, some context would help.

Idea behind log levels is to add an identifier to each trace using which we can filter specific logs, for example only "Warning" or "Error" type logs. This is similar to how generic logging implementations work.

That is ok, my question was for usability. What is the idea behind that, How are we going to use that?
a) Are you going to introduce a new mechanism to switch between levels? OR just compilation flag?
b) How will it get consumed by rest of the repositories etc.

If we need an additional mechanism for all these then I suggest you should bring all these related change as a separate commit.
This looks an overhead here.

>a) Are you going to introduce a new mechanism to switch between levels? OR just compilation flag?

Idea is that we can `grep` for specific traces from the log files. No new mechanism as such.

>How will it get consumed by rest of the repositories etc.

This implementation is for our repo right? Not going to be used by other repos.

Anyways, I have removed log level from this commit.
Blank space between the blocks to increase readability will help.
Done

We can't have a file change just for blank line in this commit.
Not relevant. May be a different commit to fix such issue?
ok. Addressed.
Done

Declare variables as an when it is used?
Now it is giving no context on how and where it will get used.

Applies to rest of the member variables as well.
Done. Some variables are being initialized in the param constructor. Kept those, removed rest.
